disposition_mapping.rationale: Document assembly is unconstrained by design and is pure precondition work with no judgment attached; it is merged into the automated match execution pipeline as its triggering sub-operation. Because real PO/GRN feeds are not universally clean or real-time (paper/Excel capture, batch-interfaced country instances, late receiving), the merged step retains a named manual-completion fallback as a first-class path, not an edge case, and preserves the same reconstructable document lineage KB-09 requires regardless of which path assembled the set.

Quantity comparison against GRN data is deterministic computation with no control checkpoint distinguishing it from the assembly and price-comparison work that already shares its actor and sequence in the baseline. It is merged into TS-01 as a separately logged sub-operation producing a distinct, named, per-line-retrievable 'quantity variance detail' output, preserving both the function (TWM-R-01) and its required GRN input (TWM-R-03) intact and inspectable rather than collapsed into an opaque match score.

Price and terms comparison against PO data is merged into TS-01 for the identical reason as quantity matching: it is deterministic, actor-identical, and sequence-adjacent in the baseline. The function (TWM-R-02) and its required PO input (TWM-R-04) are preserved as a distinct, named 'price and terms variance detail' output, with FX exchange differences kept separately visible rather than netted into a generic variance figure, consistent with IAS 21 (KB-08).

Tolerance evaluation is reorganised into its own distinct, independently auditable step rather than folded into the match engine, because it is the one point where governed policy meets data and the actual branch decision (straight-through versus exception) occurs. The tolerance policy survives as an explicit, versioned, owned input (TWM-R-05, TWM-R-06), now with a named accountable owner and periodic re-approval cadence to prevent undisclosed tolerance drift, and every classification is traceable to the policy version that produced it.

Exception investigation and resolution survives essentially unchanged in its judgment character (TWM-R-10): the decision to accept, correct or reject stays with a named, accountable AP analyst, evidenced in the record. AI assistance is permitted for investigation and drafting but is explicitly barred from executing a disposition at any materiality level, consistent with IAS 8's error-correction accountability and the near-unanimous rejection of autonomous resolution authority.

Match release approval is restructured into a tiered gate: system-executed release for clean/tolerance-passed matches, and mandatory named-human AP-supervisor approval for exception-resolved and override cases (TWM-R-07). Exception resolution continues to strictly precede authorization (TWM-R-08), and the resolver/approver separation is upgraded from organisational description to system-enforced instance-level control (TWM-R-09), closing the risk that a single identity resolves and then approves the same case.

Control reporting is restructured so that data capture is continuous and machine-native, but a controller-level human retains periodic review and attestation responsibility, now explicitly including sampling audit of straight-through-released matches (the compensating control for removing per-transaction approval in TS-04) and periodic re-approval of tolerance thresholds. Continuous logging alone was rejected by the council as a substitute for human review; the function survives as an accountable, cadence-based control, not merely a queryable dataset.

steps.actor: Automated matching engine, with AP analyst performing manual-completion fallback
steps.description: Document assembly, quantity matching and price/terms matching are run as a single triggered pipeline the instant a structured validated invoice record arrives: the engine retrieves PO and GRN data, assembles the match document set, and performs line-level quantity comparison against GRN data and price/terms comparison against PO data in one pass. These remain three separately logged sub-operations with two distinct, named, per-line-retrievable outputs (quantity variance detail; price and terms variance detail, with any FX exchange difference between PO commitment and invoice settlement separately identified) rather than a single opaque score, because quantity exceptions and price exceptions route to different remediation channels (receiving versus procurement/vendor master) and because this per-line detail is the evidentiary basis for cost under IAS 2. Where automated retrieval is incomplete, late, batch-interfaced, or paper/Excel-based at the receiving dock, an AP analyst completes the match set manually (attaching a GRN image, keying a late-arriving PO line); the manually completed set must carry the same reconstructable PO-line-to-GRN-line-to-invoice-line lineage as an automated pull. Failed or missing retrieval raises a monitored data-exception event rather than stalling or guessing.
steps.name: Automated match execution with manual-completion fallback
outputs: Assembled match document set (with reconstructable document lineage)
Price and terms variance detail (with FX exchange differences separately identified)

steps.actor: Automated tolerance engine (tolerance policy owned and periodically re-approved by AP supervisor/controller)
steps.description: Quantity and price/terms variance detail are evaluated against the tolerance policy to classify the match as clean, within tolerance, or an exception, and to route it accordingly (straight-through toward release authorization, or into exception investigation). This remains a distinct step, separate from the match execution engine, because it is the point where governed policy meets data and the actual control branch occurs; isolating it allows the tolerance policy to be versioned and audited independently of matching logic. The tolerance policy is an explicit, versioned artifact with a named accountable owner (AP supervisor or controller) who periodically re-approves thresholds; it may be locally configured to reflect market-specific FX or price volatility while remaining internally version-consistent. Every classification logs which policy version produced it, making the decision reconstructible.
steps.name: Tolerance evaluation and routing

steps.description: Matches classified as exceptions are investigated against source documents and vendor correspondence and resolved as accepted, corrected or rejected, with the resolution evidenced and attributed to a named individual. An AI investigation assistant may retrieve vendor correspondence, prior case history and PO/GRN detail and propose a draft root-cause classification and resolution with citations, but it never executes a disposition; the AP analyst's acceptance, correction or rejection is the actual control event. If the analyst accepts an AI-drafted suggestion, that acceptance is itself logged as a distinct act of judgment, not a default click-through. No materiality threshold permits an agent to resolve an exception unilaterally: resolution authority stays with the accountable human regardless of exception size, because materiality thresholds for automated resolution drift under volume pressure and a wrongly cleared low-value exception is still an uncorrected error.
steps.name: Exception investigation and resolution
outputs: Exception resolution evidence (including AI-proposal vs. human-decision distinction)

steps.actor: System-executed release (clean/tolerance lane); AP supervisor (exception-resolved and override cases)
steps.description: Clean and within-tolerance matches release on a system-executed, pre-authorised delegation-of-authority lane with no per-transaction human touch; the system enforces a hard gate preventing any match carrying an exception classification from entering this lane. Matches that passed through exception resolution, and any match requiring an override of standard tolerance, require explicit, logged approval from a named AP supervisor who reviews the full resolution evidence and variance detail, not a status flag. The actor performing exception resolution and the actor authorising release are structurally distinct, enforced at the system/identity level (the resolver of record on a given case cannot be the approver of record on that same case), not merely implied by job title. Resolution strictly precedes authorization in all cases. Any straight-through-released match remains reversible and re-openable via the exception path if a defect is later discovered.
steps.name: Match release authorization gate

steps.description: Match outcomes, tolerance overrides, exception resolutions and release authorisations are logged continuously to the control record as a native byproduct of TS-01, TS-02 and TS-04 activity, rather than transcribed in a periodic batch. A controller-level human reviews and attests the resulting match-rate and override report on a defined, auditable cadence tied to the existing control calendar; this review is the compensating control for straight-through release and must include a sampling-based human audit of a defined proportion of straight-through-released matches, to catch engine miscalibration that no individual transaction would surface. The same cadence includes periodic re-approval of tolerance policy thresholds to prevent undisclosed tolerance creep. Continuous machine logging strengthens the evidential trail but does not substitute for the human attestation; a ledger nobody is accountable for reviewing is not a control.
steps.name: Match control reporting, sampling audit and policy governance
outputs: Sampling audit findings on straight-through releases
Tolerance policy review and re-approval record
